description: Erection of a double storey rear extension and then the  change of use from C3 to C4
decision_conditions:
<p><span style="font-size: 14px;">﻿</span><span style="font-size: 14px; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">In
the absence of a Flood Risk Assessment incorporating SuDS, the application
fails to demonstrate that the proposed development would be safe for its
lifetime or that it would not increase flood risk on‑site or elsewhere. The
proposal involves the loss of existing soft landscaping and the introduction of
additional hard surfacing, which has the potential to increase surface‑water
runoff and reduce natural infiltration.&nbsp; The proposal therefore conflicts
with Policies F15.7 (Flood Risk Management and Sustainable Drainage), F15.8
(Managing Local Flooding) and F15.9 (Sustainable Drainage Systems) of the
Merton Local Plan.</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 14px;">﻿</span><span style="font-size: 14px; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">It
has not been satisfactorily demonstrated that adequate provision h</span><span style="font-size: 14px;">﻿</span><span style="font-size: 14px; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">as been made
for the storage of waste, or that the development would not result in
obstruction of the highway, increased street clutter, or harm to residential
amenity. The proposal therefore conflicts with the requirements of the Merton
Local Plan, including Policies D12.2, D12.3 and T16.3.</span></p>

<p>The proposals by reason of absence of detailed internal layout plan results in an unsatisfactory layout that would create a poor standard of accommodation and internal environment for occupiers of the C4 HMO. The proposal would therefore be contrary to policy D6 of the London Plan 2021 and policy D12.3 of Merton's Local Plan 2024</p>

<p>The proposed first floor rear extension by reason of its combined siting, height, depth and design results in an incongruous form of development that would disrupt the uniform first floor rear building line of the terrace row that it forms a part of to the detriment of the appearance of the terrace row.&nbsp; The proposal is contrary to, in particular, policy D12.2, D12.3 and D12.4 of Merton Local Plan (2024).</p>
<p>The development would result in the loss of a family sized unit thereby failing to comply with policy H11.1 of Merton Local Plan 2024.</p>

<p><span style="line-height:1"><span style="font-size:11pt; text-align:justify"><span style="vertical-align:top">The proposed part two part single storey rear extension by reason of its combined height, depth and siting results in an overbearing and visually intrusive form of development that would adversely impact on outlook and potentially daylight/sunlight from the adjoining residents, in particular, no. 118 High Street, contrary to Policy D12.4 of Merton Local Plan (2024).</span></span></span></p>

<p>By reason of absence of sufficient secure, integrated, convenient and accessible cycle parking facilities and absence of a s106 legal agreement to restrict access of future occupiers from obtaining residents parking permit, the scheme will impact the free flow of traffic in the locality to the detriment of highway and pedestrian safety and is contrary to, in particular, policy T16.2 of Merton's Local Plan 2024 and T5 of the London Plan 2021.</p>
